title: Sequential Spinodal Decompositions and Ordering Reactions in an As-Quenched Cr<sub>39</sub>Co<sub>18</sub>Fe<sub>18</sub>Ni<sub>18</sub>Al<sub>7</sub> High-Entropy Alloy.

recollection.intervention: Isothermal aging between 600–800 °C for up to 100 h, tracked by DSC, XRD and TEM (guess)
recollection.structure: Nanoscale compositional modulations that develop into B2-ordered (Al–Co–rich) precipitates in an FCC matrix (guess)
recollection.mechanism: Two-stage sequence: initial spinodal decomposition driven by atomic‐size and enthalpy fluctuations, followed by ordering of Al–Co–rich regions into a B2 structure (guess)
recollection.results: After 100 h at 700 °C, precipitate spacing ≈10–20 nm, activation energy ≈180 kJ/mol, and hardness rise from ≈300 HV to ≈450 HV (guess)

score.note: The proposed 600–800 °C long-term aging treatment is incorrect; the study used brief anneals at 1100–1300 °C followed by water quenching. The recollection incorrectly places Al–Co-rich B2 precipitates in an FCC matrix rather than describing reciprocal Ni–Al-rich B2/Ni–Al-lean BCC structures in a mainly BCC matrix. The spinodal-decomposition-then-ordering sequence is broadly consistent with the title, but its stated chemical driver is wrong and adds little correct detail beyond the title. All reported times, sizes, activation energy, and hardness values are unsupported or incorrect.
